mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate above 4.0% compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 unemployment rate rising from 4.1% to 7.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by >0.5pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand that triggers corporate profit warnings and negative equity returns over 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 HOUST at 1256k and RSAFS at 715.4B
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index level during recessionary conditions signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth and drives negative equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer price index exceeding 300 indicates elevated inflation that triggers aggressive monetary policy tightening, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: A total non-farm payrolls level below 160,000 (thousands) indicates labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS < 160,000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate severe consumer demand contraction that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 HOUST at 1256k and GDPC1 at 23512.7B
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and GDPC1 does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) combined with CPIAUCSL > 300 during high-inflation regimes signals aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:2008 FEDFUNDS at 4.33% and CPI at 321.5
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 300.
